questions.q: What gap in Chapters 1–3's controls (roles, ACLs, SSO, MFA) does Edge Encryption address?
options: None of those controls change the fact that ServiceNow itself can read a field's plaintext value once it's written
Roles and ACLs are too slow to evaluate on large tables
SSO and MFA cannot be combined with ACLs
Edge Encryption replaces the need for any role or ACL design
questions.explain: Roles, ACLs, SSO, and MFA all control who can reach data and how they authenticate — none of them stop the platform vendor itself from being able to read a stored plaintext value.

questions.q: Where does Edge Encryption actually encrypt a sensitive field's value?
options: Inside the customer's own network, via a customer-side proxy, before the value ever reaches ServiceNow's cloud
Inside ServiceNow's cloud infrastructure, immediately after the request arrives
Only inside the user's browser cache
It does not encrypt the value at all, only the connection
questions.explain: Edge Encryption places an encryption proxy in the customer's own network, encrypting the value before it ever leaves that network — so only ciphertext ever reaches ServiceNow's servers.

questions.q: How does column-level encryption differ from Edge Encryption?
options: Column-level encryption protects data at rest in the database but doesn't prevent the application layer from decrypting it during normal processing, unlike Edge Encryption's customer-side approach
Column-level encryption is simply a faster version of Edge Encryption
Column-level encryption requires a customer-side proxy, while Edge Encryption does not
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: Column-level encryption guards against storage-level exposure (backups, direct database access), but the application still decrypts the value to use it — a narrower guarantee than Edge Encryption's.

questions.q: What is the real, practical tradeoff of encrypting a field?
options: Platform features that depend on reading the plaintext — full-text search, certain reports, some integrations — stop working correctly on that field
Encrypted fields become permanently read-only for every role
Encryption has no effect on any platform feature
Encrypted fields can no longer be included on any form
questions.explain: Because the platform can't meaningfully search, filter, or aggregate against ciphertext, features relying on the real value behave differently once a field is encrypted — a cost to weigh against the sensitivity of that specific field.

questions.q: Why is blanket-encrypting every field on an instance a poor approach, per this lesson?
options: It breaks search, reporting, and automation across many fields in exchange for little real security benefit on fields that weren't actually sensitive
ServiceNow technically limits instances to five encrypted fields total
Encryption can only be applied to one table per instance
It has no downside at all and is actually the recommended default
questions.explain: Encryption should be applied deliberately to genuinely sensitive fields, not broadly — otherwise you pay the functionality cost everywhere without a matching security benefit.
